notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Job 5, because the research tools failed and I wasn't able to read a single page.

**What happened:**
- My first attempt to fetch five pages was refused because I'd hit a usage limit.
- After that, every web search and page fetch timed out. That included enduringword.com, a plain "Job 5 commentary" search, and even a basic test of the tool.
- The sandbox itself works; it has no internet access, so it can't get around the problem.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from memory. So I haven't written verse notes, quoted any commentators or given any URLs, since none of it would come from pages I read.

**What I'll do once the tools are working:**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Job 5, the Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill and Barnes commentaries on Bible Hub and StudyLight, and Precept Austin's Job pages.
2. **Where traditions differ:** v. 13 is the likely main point. Paul quotes it in 1 Corinthians 3:19, which sits awkwardly with God saying in Job 42:7 that the friends hadn't spoken rightly. I'd check how Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Lutheran and Pentecostal teachers on the allowed sites handle that, and how they treat vv. 17–18 on God's discipline.
3. **Other views:**
   - the translators' notes on netbible.org (likely helpful on the hard Hebrew in vv. 1, 3, 5 and 7);
   - background articles on bibleodyssey.org;
   - Gregory the Great's *Moralia on Job* (an early Christian commentary) on newadvent.org or ccel.org;
   - articles on gotquestions.org or the Reformed and Baptist sites that criticise prosperity teaching, which may cover how Eliphaz's promises in vv. 19–26 get used.

To try again, just say "retry." If the tools are still unreliable, I can do one source at a time, starting with Enduring Word and the NET notes.
